title: Research Methods in Sociology
topics: Ethics and the politics of research

items.q: Which term is described by “a testable expectation about a relationship between two or more attributes”?
o: Research design
Pilot test
Cross-sectional plan
Hypothesis
items.s: Hypothesis is a testable expectation about a relationship between two or more attributes.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Statistical significance?
o: the inclination to give answers that will be viewed favourably by others
the judgement that an observed pattern is unlikely to have arisen from chance alone
a grid showing the joint distribution of two categorical attributes
a well-placed person who can explain the workings of a setting to an outsider
items.s: Statistical significance: the judgement that an observed pattern is unlikely to have arisen from chance alone. The other options describe Cross-tabulation, Social desirability, Key informant.

items.q: The statement “the use of more than one source, procedure or analyst to check a conclusion” describes which of the following?
o: Comparative method
Secondary data
Triangulation
Official statistics
items.s: Triangulation is the use of more than one source, procedure or analyst to check a conclusion.

items.q: Problem statement may be defined as
o: the entire set of units about which a conclusion is wanted
the position that collective behaviour can be recorded with the same procedures used for natural phenomena
a short passage establishing what is not yet known about a topic and why the gap matters
the duty to keep those taking part free of physical or psychological injury
items.s: Problem statement: a short passage establishing what is not yet known about a topic and why the gap matters. The other options describe Protection from harm, Population, Positivist stance.

items.q: Unit of analysis may be defined as
o: the allocation of cases to conditions by chance so that the sets begin alike
the entity, such as a person, household or event, that a statement is about
the extension of a finding beyond the units actually observed
the running written record made while in a setting or soon after leaving it
items.s: Unit of analysis: the entity, such as a person, household or event, that a statement is about. The other options describe Field notes, Generalisation, Random assignment.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Confidence interval?
o: a range around an estimate within which the true value probably lies
the position that conduct can only be understood by grasping the meanings actors attach to it
figures collected routinely by government agencies for administrative purposes
the trust that allows people to speak freely with an enquirer
items.s: Confidence interval: a range around an estimate within which the true value probably lies. The other options describe Official statistics, Interpretive stance, Rapport.

items.q: The statement “a systematic count or classification of what appears in texts or images” describes which of the following?
o: Official statistics
Secondary data
Content analysis
Triangulation
items.s: Content analysis is a systematic count or classification of what appears in texts or images.

items.q: Which term is described by “the set that receives the intervention whose effect is being gauged”?
o: Controlled trial
Random assignment
Treatment group
Quasi-experiment
items.s: Treatment group is the set that receives the intervention whose effect is being gauged.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Acquiescence.
o: the acknowledged weaknesses that bound what the findings can support
the tendency to agree with an item whatever its content
a set of labels that differ in kind only, with no order implied between them
the position that collective behaviour can be recorded with the same procedures used for natural phenomena
items.s: Acquiescence: the tendency to agree with an item whatever its content. The other options describe Nominal category, Positivist stance, Limitations.

items.q: All of the following belong to Selecting cases EXCEPT
o: Treatment group
Sample
Sampling frame
Population
items.s: Every other option belongs to Selecting cases. “Treatment group” belongs to Experiments and evaluation, not Selecting cases.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Variable?
o: an observable item treated as evidence of a condition that cannot be seen directly
the list or map from which units are actually chosen
agreement given by someone who understands the purpose and the risks
any characteristic that can take different values across cases or over time
items.s: Variable: any characteristic that can take different values across cases or over time. The other options describe Sampling frame, Informed consent, Indicator.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Scale.
o: a graded set of replies arranged so that greater strength can be ranked
the running written record made while in a setting or soon after leaving it
the sorting of passages under recurring topics that the material itself suggests
a grid showing the joint distribution of two categorical attributes
items.s: Scale: a graded set of replies arranged so that greater strength can be ranked. The other options describe Field notes, Cross-tabulation, Thematic grouping.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Index?
o: a systematic count or classification of what appears in texts or images
a printed list of items that a trained fieldworker reads aloud and records
the undertaking that identifying details will not be passed on to others
a single score produced by adding or averaging several separate items
items.s: Index: a single score produced by adding or averaging several separate items. The other options describe Confidentiality, Content analysis, Interview schedule.

items.q: Field notes may be defined as
o: a ranking with equal gaps and a true zero, so that doubling is meaningful
the enquirer's scrutiny of how their own position shapes what they notice and report
the running written record made while in a setting or soon after leaving it
material gathered by someone else for another purpose and re-used for a new analysis
items.s: Field notes: the running written record made while in a setting or soon after leaving it. The other options describe Reflexivity, Ratio measure, Secondary data.

items.q: Anonymity may be defined as
o: the statement of the exact steps by which an abstract idea will be observed
a statement answered on a graded set of agreement options from strongly agree to strongly disagree
the condition in which even the enquirer cannot link a reply to a particular person
prolonged immersion in a setting so that its routine is learned from inside
items.s: Anonymity: the condition in which even the enquirer cannot link a reply to a particular person. The other options describe Operationalisation, Ethnography, Likert scale.
items.t: Ethics and the politics of research

items.q: The statement “the consistency of a procedure, giving the same reading when used again” describes which of the following?
o: Variable
Ratio measure
Nominal category
Reliability
items.s: Reliability is the consistency of a procedure, giving the same reading when used again.

items.q: The statement “a measure of how far two attributes rise and fall in step” describes which of the following?
o: Sampling error
Regression
Confidence interval
Correlation
items.s: Correlation is a measure of how far two attributes rise and fall in step.

items.q: The statement “the systematic contrast of two or more settings to isolate what makes them differ” describes which of the following?
o: Comparative method
Diary method
Triangulation
Discourse analysis
items.s: Comparative method is the systematic contrast of two or more settings to isolate what makes them differ.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Longitudinal plan?
o: an arrangement that returns to the same units again and again over years
repetition of a piece of work by others to see whether the result holds
the entire set of units about which a conclusion is wanted
a testable expectation about a relationship between two or more attributes
items.s: Longitudinal plan: an arrangement that returns to the same units again and again over years. The other options describe Population, Replication, Hypothesis.

items.q: The statement “recruiting further participants through the introductions of those already studied” describes which of the following?
o: Unit of analysis
Referral chain
Equal-chance draw
Cluster draw
items.s: Referral chain is recruiting further participants through the introductions of those already studied.

items.q: Quasi-experiment may be defined as
o: a comparison of naturally formed groups where allocation was not controlled
the judgement that an observed pattern is unlikely to have arisen from chance alone
the position that collective behaviour can be recorded with the same procedures used for natural phenomena
picking whole groups such as schools or wards first, then studying those within them
items.s: Quasi-experiment: a comparison of naturally formed groups where allocation was not controlled. The other options describe Statistical significance, Cluster draw, Positivist stance.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Index?
o: a well-placed person who can explain the workings of a setting to an outsider
a prompt offering a fixed set of replies from which one must be chosen
a single score produced by adding or averaging several separate items
recruiting further participants through the introductions of those already studied
items.s: Index: a single score produced by adding or averaging several separate items. The other options describe Key informant, Closed item, Referral chain.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cross-sectional plan?
o: dividing the population into homogeneous layers and picking separately within each
the trust that allows people to speak freely with an enquirer
an arrangement in which all observations are taken at a single point in time
the use of more than one source, procedure or analyst to check a conclusion
items.s: Cross-sectional plan: an arrangement in which all observations are taken at a single point in time. The other options describe Triangulation, Rapport, Stratified draw.

items.q: Social desirability may be defined as
o: the consistency of a procedure, giving the same reading when used again
the point at which further material stops producing new categories
the inclination to give answers that will be viewed favourably by others
a ranking with equal gaps and a true zero, so that doubling is meaningful
items.s: Social desirability: the inclination to give answers that will be viewed favourably by others. The other options describe Ratio measure, Reliability, Saturation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Likert scale.
o: a ranking with equal gaps but a zero point fixed by convention rather than by absence
the entire set of units about which a conclusion is wanted
a statement answered on a graded set of agreement options from strongly agree to strongly disagree
the change in people's conduct caused by knowing that they are being watched
items.s: Likert scale: a statement answered on a graded set of agreement options from strongly agree to strongly disagree. The other options describe Population, Interval measure, Observer effect.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Sampling frame?
o: inquiry carried out with the people concerned so that practice changes as it proceeds
the reasoned account of why a chosen set of procedures suits a particular kind of question
the condition in which even the enquirer cannot link a reply to a particular person
the list or map from which units are actually chosen
items.s: Sampling frame: the list or map from which units are actually chosen. The other options describe Methodology, Action research, Anonymity.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Protection from harm.
o: the extension of a finding beyond the units actually observed
the reasoned account of why a chosen set of procedures suits a particular kind of question
the duty to keep those taking part free of physical or psychological injury
figures collected routinely by government agencies for administrative purposes
items.s: Protection from harm: the duty to keep those taking part free of physical or psychological injury. The other options describe Generalisation, Methodology, Official statistics.
items.t: Ethics and the politics of research

items.q: The statement “the duty to keep those taking part free of physical or psychological injury” describes which of the following?

Protection from harm
Informed consent
Confidentiality
items.s: Protection from harm is the duty to keep those taking part free of physical or psychological injury.

items.q: The statement “the estimation of how much one attribute shifts for a unit change in another” describes which of the following?
o: Regression
Correlation
Coding
Statistical significance
items.s: Regression is the estimation of how much one attribute shifts for a unit change in another.

the consistency of a procedure, giving the same reading when used again
a printed list of items that a trained fieldworker reads aloud and records
a measure of how far two attributes rise and fall in step

the basic procedure that gives every unit on the list an identical probability of inclusion
the undertaking that identifying details will not be passed on to others

the proportion of those approached who return usable returns
a well-placed person who can explain the workings of a setting to an outsider

items.q: Which term is described by “a ranking with equal gaps but a zero point fixed by convention rather than by absence”?

Nominal category

items.q: Which term is described by “a standardised set of items put to many people in the same way”?

Survey

material gathered by someone else for another purpose and re-used for a new analysis

items.q: Open item may be defined as
o: the position that collective behaviour can be recorded with the same procedures used for natural phenomena
a prompt that allows the person answering to use their own words
the comparison set that does not receive the intervention
a person who controls an outsider's access to a group or institution
items.s: Open item: a prompt that allows the person answering to use their own words. The other options describe Positivist stance, Control group, Gatekeeper.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Deception?

items.q: The statement “a long, loosely guided conversation that invites a person to talk at length” describes which of the following?

In-depth interview
Key informant
Field notes
items.s: In-depth interview is a long, loosely guided conversation that invites a person to talk at length.

a written schedule of items that the person completing it fills in unaided
a ranking with equal gaps but a zero point fixed by convention rather than by absence
the position that collective behaviour can be recorded with the same procedures used for natural phenomena

a small rehearsal run used to find faults in instruments before the main fieldwork
